newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean police raid German enclave.
newsitem.headline: Chilean police raid German enclave.

text.p: Police raided on Wednesday a secretive German colony in southern Chile in search of its fugitive leader Paul Schaefer, who is accused of sexually molesting boys in the colony.
Local radio reported that 150 police moved shortly after dawn into the enclave known as Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony) near the town of Parral.
The raid, part of a government investigation allegations of child sexual abuse and kidnapping within the colony, could last several hours, said the radio.

The government was confident that Schaefer, the German-speaking colony's founder who was believed to be holed up in the heavily guarded community, would soon be arrested, said Interior Deputy Secretary Belisario Velasco.
"Schaefer will be detained sooner rather than later," said Velasco.
Velasco said he believed that there could be unregistered weapons in the colony which lies tucked in the foothills of the Andes, around 200 miles (340 km) south of Santiago.
Police arrested late on Tuesday two members of the colony, Hartmuth Hopp and Gerhard Zevalt, on charges they had refused to appear in court to give evidence in the case against Schaefer.

Schaefer, who has not been seen in public in recent years, faced charges of sexually molesting at least five Chilean boys who attended a boarding school at Colonia Dignidad. He and other leaders also faced charges of illegal detention of children and obstruction of justice.

The raid came several days after a man pretending to be Paul Schaefer checked into a hotel in Bariloche in southern Argentine, but that proved to be a ploy to distract attention from the colony, said Chilean government officials.
Congressmen welcomed news of the raid, saying Chileans have long been waiting for the government to take such firm measures to search the colony.
"I think that what we are seeing is what public opinion has been expecting for a long time. At last this is happening," said socialist deputy Jaime Naranjo.
Naranjo said he believed the police decided to act now as many of the journalists who have been staking out the colony for the last few weeks have now left the area.
Schaefer, who is believed to be in his 80s, founded the colony was founded in 1961.
Human rights groups have charged the settlement was used as a detention centre in the 1970s for political prisoners during General Augusto Pinochet's military rule.
